title: The system: a flash sale where one item gets most of the traffic
caption: Sharding spreads keys, not requests: one popular key still lands on one shard, so the design adds detection, local copies and split counters.

steps.text: A limited sneaker drop opens at 10:00. The CDN serves the page shell and images; only the item data and checkout calls reach the backend.
The product API reads items from a sharded cache. Every request for item 777 hashes to the same key, so they all land on shard 2.
Each API pod samples the keys it reads and reports counts every second. The detector keeps a top-K and marks keys far above the rest as hot.
Hot keys are served from each pod's memory for 1 s. Shard 2 now sees about one read per pod per second instead of every request; one refill per key per pod at a time.
Checkout needs a correct count, not a cached one: stock is split into 8 parts on different shards, each holding a share. A checkout decrements one part and tries another when it's empty.
Reserved orders go to a queue and are written to the orders DB at the pace it can take.

scenarios.name: Unplanned viral item
scenarios.summary: A celebrity posts a link to a different item with no warning. The system is unprotected until the detector catches up.

steps.text: Traffic to item 512 goes from nothing to a large share of all reads within a minute.
Its key lives on shard 1, whose CPU climbs while the other shards idle.
Within a few seconds the samples show it; the detector adds it to the hot list and pods start serving it locally.
Shard 1 drops back to normal load. The gap between spike and detection is the window to keep short.

scenarios.name: Hot shard saturates
scenarios.summary: Before mitigation kicks in, the hot shard slows down for every key it owns, not just the hot one.

steps.text: Shard 2 hits 100% CPU on item 777 and starts timing out.
Thousands of unrelated items that also hash to shard 2 now time out too: the collateral damage of a hot key.
Pods trip a circuit breaker for shard 2 and serve stale local copies where they have them, rather than retrying and making it worse.
Misses for shard-2 keys fall back to the catalog DB within a concurrency cap until the hot list takes the load off.

scenarios.name: Pre-warm before the drop
scenarios.summary: Planned events don't have to wait for detection: mark the keys hot ahead of time.

steps.text: An hour before 10:00 an operator adds item 777 to the hot list with a 2-hour expiry.
Pods load it into local memory before the first shopper arrives.
The stock is pre-split into its 8 parts, so checkout never touches a single counter.
